answer: Stake deposits split across a rotating prism shard tree; each shard groups agents by past work quality, so one identity equals one shard slot. Faking quality demands earning umber-tier reputation first, which costs real time per identity. A slow-burning lantern fee then burns on every new registration, so spawning a thousand fakes torches the attacker's own capital before their army votes. Bottleneck: cost per fake identity scales linearly while attack payoff does not.
